notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, survey and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 5 simply supported 50-ft bays, W36X529 girders, one 35-ton cab crane, on new welded haunched rib seats welded to the existing W14X257 columns, with the rail, ties, bearings and end stops; the existing columns are checked with their existing load effects and the existing sidewall rod bracing takes the crane longitudinal forces. A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-weld-fatigue 2.71, flange-tie-saddle-weld 2.51 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class B)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.5 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusset; checks tie-slide-*). Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.designed: Paired flat bars on a bearing-stiffener gusset
selections.reason: A direct flange saddle does not suit this rolled girder (the sized saddle leaves flange-tie-weld-fatigue 2.71, flange-tie-saddle-weld 2.51 for the estimated tie demands; a welded saddle is a Category D/E attachment on the top flange of this high-cycle runway (CMAA Class D, AIST Class B)): the paired flat bars bolt to the tie-side bearing stiffener, cut as one plate with its gusset extension past the flange tip (no weld at the gusset), the full-depth stiffener pair carrying the tie force into the girder. Fixed at both ends at this reach, the paired bars cannot follow the girder end rotation and thermal travel along the runway (the tie movement checks over their limits): the column gusset slides 0.5 in each way along the runway on longer sleeves (column-end slide, fillers at the girder gusse

No compact W meets every sizing target; the closest: top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 1.12, vertical deflection 0.66 and lateral 1.23 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 113 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X487: tips ratio 1.36 > 0.85; lateral deflection 1.36 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios. A built-up plate girder is required: the closest section is built and calculated, and the package is a review draft (open item).

Fictitious example existing column for a 35-ton crane (W14X90 to 7.5 t, W14X120 to 15 t, W14X159 to 30 t, else W14X211); replace with the surveyed shape. The W14X211 column flange at the bracket rib weld toes has a fatigue ratio 1.04 > 0.9 (AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1, the bracket moment range on the column section at all cycles): the lightest heavier W14 within it, 0.85.
Set by the tie sizing: the column face moves out from 20 in (to at most 30 in) until the tie passes its imposed-movement and strength checks.

Weld-on clip bases on the top flange are an AISC Table A-3.1 item 7.1 attachment, Category D: the estimated top-plate range 16.79 ksi (rated-lift crane moment without impact plus the top-flange lateral bending under the side thrust) at all 500,000 cycles exceeds F_SR = 16.39 ksi (ratio 1.02, the project's all-cycle method). Bolted clamp plates leave holes for pretensioned bolts (item 2.2, Category B), as AISC DG7 and AIST TR-13 allow.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints thermite or flash-butt welded by the rail supplier's qualified procedure (preheat, grinding, inspection); no joint bars or bolts.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
